A database index is like the index at the back of a cookbook. Without it, finding every recipe that uses basil means turning every page. With it, you look up "basil", read the page numbers, and go straight to those pages.

What it's actually doing: the database keeps a separate, sorted list of the values in one column (say, customer email), and next to each value it writes where that row is kept. A search for one email checks the short sorted list instead of reading the whole table.

The cost: every new recipe means updating the cookbook's index too, so adding rows gets a little slower in exchange for much faster lookups.

That's the plain version, want the high-school one?
